extractions.value: Patient had synchronized spinal segmental myoclonus in both legs. Initially presented with LRP4 antibody-positive symptoms (dysphagia, vocal cord paralysis) treated as myasthenia gravis-like illness before developing PERM at age 74. Bilateral ptosis and diplopia developed 2 months after PERM treatment, attributed to PERM rather than myasthenia gravis (negative repeat MG testing).
extractions.quote: We describe a patient with PERM associated with GlyR-Abs who had synchronized spinal segmental myoclonus in both legs. [...] indicating that these features were derived from PREM.
